title: Yudhishthira's dog
hook: at the top of the world, a god offers Yudhishthira heaven on one condition: leave the dog behind
carry: the divine in every creature, even a dog
tomorrow: what does Yudhishthira find when he reaches heaven?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Arjuna fell, then Bhima, for eating with no thought of others, and Yudhishthira walked on with only the dog. Your line was prasad, food offered first, then shared.
screen: `THE LAST JOURNEY.` · `ONE BY ONE THEY FALL.`

segments.voice: Two of them are left on the mountain: a king and a dog. Yudhishthira's brothers have fallen behind him. Draupadi has fallen. The dog that joined them at the start of the road is still at his heel. Then the sky fills with sound, and Indra, king of the gods, pulls up in a chariot. Climb in, he says. Heaven is waiting. This is the moment the whole road has led to. And in Ganguli's telling, Yudhishthira's first answer is not yes. It's a question about who gets to come with him.
screen: `A KING AND A DOG.` → `INDRA'S CHARIOT ARRIVES.` → `"CLIMB IN."`

segments.voice: First he asks about his brothers and Draupadi; he won't go without them. Indra reassures him: they left their bodies on the way and are already in heaven. You, he says, will go up in yours. Then Yudhishthira says the dog has been devoted to him, and it should come too. Indra says no. You have won heaven and a state like a god's. Leave the dog; there is no cruelty in that. Heaven has no place for people with dogs. Notice how reasonable it sounds. It's only a dog, the offer is enormous, and no one else will speak for it. Yudhishthira refuses. Turning away one who is devoted to you, who is frightened and has nowhere else to go, he says, is a grave wrong, and he will not do it even for his own happiness. Then the dog changes. It is Dharma, the god of righteousness, Yudhishthira's own father, walking beside him in disguise. Dharma praises him and recalls an earlier test at a forest lake, when Yudhishthira chose to bring back Nakula, son of his father's other wife, out of fairness. Only then does he climb into the chariot. Now the twist. In the old purity rules a dog counted as unclean, and Indra's words echo that. Yet Dharma himself chose that shape. The Gita says the wise see the same in a learned priest, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and an outcast. One self, in the king and in the dog.
screen: `"NOT WITHOUT MY BROTHERS"` · `INDRA: LEAVE THE DOG` · `"I WILL NOT TURN IT AWAY"` · `THE DOG IS DHARMA` · then, large: `THE SAME SELF IN EVERY CREATURE`

segments.voice: Find one living creature near you: a pet, a bird outside the window, a person across the room. For a minute, just look at it, without naming it useful or annoying, clean or dirty. As you breathe, think: the same life that's in me is in this one. If you pray, you can see the Lord there; if not, simply see the creature.
Dharma. The god of righteousness, who walked beside Yudhishthira the whole way as a dog, and revealed himself only at the gate of heaven.
Keep this one: the divine in every creature, even a dog. Tomorrow, heaven is not what he expects. Thanks for sitting with me.

howItsDone: The story of Yudhishthira and the dog comes from the Mahaprasthanika Parva and is retold in recitations of the epic. The Gita's teaching that the wise see the same self in every creature is often quoted alongside it, and in Nepal the second day of Tihar, Kukur Tihar, honors dogs with garlands and a tilak.

notes: All paraphrase of Ganguli. Lines in quotation marks on screen are plain-English glosses of speech, not quotations.
Confirm Indra's reply that the brothers and Draupadi have gone ahead having cast off their bodies, while Yudhishthira ascends in his own body.

Confirm the gloss of Yudhishthira's refusal (abandoning one who is devoted, frightened and without other refuge is a grave wrong; he will not abandon it for his own happiness). Ganguli compares the sin to slaying a brahmana; that comparison was left out here.
Confirm Indra's line that heaven has no place for persons with dogs, and that he says there is no cruelty in leaving it.
Confirm that Dharma recalls the earlier test at the lake in the Dvaita forest, where Yudhishthira chose Nakula for the sake of Madri.
